Modified assessment using the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) as context:
- Macro and policy: The FOMC raised the target range to 5.25–5.50 percent and continues balance-sheet runoff, consistent with a restrictive stance amid elevated inflation and robust recent job gains.
- Bank credit supply: The July 2023 SLOOS reports broad-based tightening of lending standards across commercial and consumer credit: C&I and syndicated loans; commercial real estate (construction, land development, and nonfarm nonresidential); residential real estate (GSE-eligible, jumbo, and government mortgages); HELOCs; and consumer credit (credit cards and auto). Banks also tightened terms on credit cards and auto loans.
- Credit demand: SLOOS indicates weaker demand for subprime mortgage loans, reinforcing a softer credit impulse.
- Implications: The survey corroborates the Committee’s warning that tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity and hiring. Compared with a headline read of the statement, SLOOS evidence points to a stronger drag from bank intermediation, increasing downside growth risks even as it supports disinflation.

Net: Cautious tilt, slightly negative given broad tightening in bank credit.
